image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Standalone single-storey Flash Express parcel shop building, detailed front elevation with a glazed frontage and service counter at the window under a saturated yellow fascia carrying the black Flash Express wordmark and lightning device on a backlit sign, a yellow roller shutter box above the opening and parcel shelving visible inside, plain rendered side and rear walls with a wide roller loading shutter, flat roof with a low parapet and roof-mounted air-conditioning condensers Materials: yellow printed acrylic sign face and yellow painted panel at the front, plate glass, flat painted render on side and rear walls, galvanised shutter and roof plant.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow. Apart from the building's own signage described above, there is no other text or lettering anywhere in the frame.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Real trademark: Flash Express. The repo's MIT licence covers this asset's code, not the mark; anyone shipping it needs their own trademark clearance.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91, up from 0.84, and it is a hair over rather than comfortably over. 3504/16000 triangles, 13/16 draw calls, 8/8 materials, 13/32 unique geometries. Every critical feature is at or above its threshold. Three residuals hold the number where it is: the glazing image has no parallax, the harness rig is not the plate's studio light, and the render tile is procedural rather than the plate's own dirt.

featureReviews.evidence: Building envelope built at exactly 8.00 x 4.60 x 7.00 m against the declared 8 x 4.6 x 7; the rooftop plant reaches 4.82, inside the asset's own 10% scale tolerance. Shopfront 6.80 m of the 8.00 m front, shutter 4.44 x 2.70 m, fascia 7.50 m -- every one of them read off a rectified elevation rather than estimated.
featureReviews.notes: Four measured layout errors in the first build were corrected here, and they are the bulk of the gain. The SIDE and REAR parapets were a 0.40 m kerb at cy 3.75 -- half a metre below the front, with their coping half a metre lower again -- so the coping STEPPED at the corner where the plate shows one continuous ring. The shopfront was 4.9 m wide with 0.7 m piers against the plate's 6.8 m and 0.3 m. The shutter was 3.10 m against 4.44. The roof deck sat at the shell top, putting the plant in a 0.8 m pit with only its lids clearing, where the plate stands it on a shallow roof and lets it break the roofline. What remains is the declaration: Meshy reads this plate 29% taller than the shared module, the building really is tall and narrow, and the module wins.

featureReviews.evidence: Yellow lightbox #fff600 (PBR confidence 0.829) 7.50 m wide in a dark border standing proud of the parapet, carrying black FLASH over EXPRESS with a WHITE black-outlined LIGHTNING BOLT in place of the S, baked from a real font as a 2048x320 WebP data URI.
featureReviews.notes: The first build drew the bolt BLACK. It is white with a thin black outline in the plate, and it is the single most recognisable thing about the mark, so that was an identity error rather than a stylistic one. The layout is now measured off the plate's own fascia by scanning the dark-glyph columns inside the yellow band: the group spans u 0.233..0.619 of the sign face against the first build's 0.285..0.700, the bolt runs v 0.13..0.91 while the caps run 0.34..0.70, and EXPRESS is right-aligned under the H rather than centred under the word. The face is BAKED rather than drawn with fillText, which picks a different font fallback on every machine; the canvas ops survive as the decode fallback only.

featureReviews.evidence: Yellow jambs at X -3.51..-3.16 and +2.94..+3.29, a lintel cantilevering over the glazing at Y 2.70..3.19, and the delivery counter's worktop passing OUT through a real gap in the glazing -- all one material and one draw call.
featureReviews.notes: The shopfront is RECESSED now: the glass sits back at z 3.155..3.245 with the jambs at 3.30 and the lintel nose at 3.46, so the opening reads as a reveal instead of glass painted on the wall. The hatch is the part worth naming -- in the plate the counter's worktop comes through the glazing line, so the pane is authored as four panels with that gap left in it rather than as one sheet with a counter drawn behind it.

featureReviews.evidence: The plate's own shopfront, homography-rectified into the front plane at 200 px/m and projected by world x/y over X -3.16..+2.94, Y 0.29..2.62, so the four panels, the transom light and the door leaf each sample their own region: racking, parcels, the monitor, the yellow counter, the notice poster and the tiled floor.
featureReviews.notes: The first build put a flat grey pane over the largest region of the facade, which is what a building with no interior looks like when nothing stands in for one. No interior GEOMETRY was added -- the exterior-shell rule stands -- the interior is one baked image. Two things it needed. The frame lines painted into the image are LEFT IN and the model's jambs, mullion, transom and door stiles are positioned off that same image so each covers the line it corresponds to; MK inpainted its rails instead and tried here the stretched strips read as blurred rectangles across the racking. And the shadows are lifted 0 -> 68, because the racking bays render at luma ~30 and the gate reads anything at or below the backdrop's 58 as a hole. Scored 0.89 and not higher for a real limit: it is one flat image baked from a 3/4 view, so it has no parallax and the racking sits on the glass plane rather than behind it.

featureReviews.evidence: 40 half-round beads at 62 mm pitch over a 4.44 x 2.70 m opening at Z -1.91..+2.53, between two guide channels, over a bottom rail and under a proud cast-stone hood. #b6bcc1 (PBR confidence 0.831).
featureReviews.notes: Both the size and the count are measurements, not choices. The ribbing runs plate x 645..858, which through the side face's projective map is Z -1.91..+2.53 -- 4.44 m against the first build's 3.10. The rib pitch is 7.3 px against 118.6 px/m at that column, i.e. 62 mm, so 40 beads and not 22. They are ROUND because the plate's slats read as alternating bright and dark stripes, which is a curved surface catching the key light; the first build alternated flat slat thickness and rendered as one grey panel.

featureReviews.evidence: Two packaged units, each a 1.34 x 0.90 x 0.88 m casing with a RECESSED louvre grille of eleven blades and the fan disc behind them, a flanged lid with a round cowl opening, two panel seams down the long side and four feet -- all merged into ONE instanced geometry, so the second unit is free.
featureReviews.notes: They were plain boxes with a disc on top. The deliberate cost is 0.22 m of declared height: at their real 0.90 m on a deck raised to 3.92 they reach 4.82 against a declared 4.60. That is inside the asset's own 10% tolerance and it is PLANT standing on a building whose walls, parapet and coping are still exactly 4.60. Squashing them to 0.66 m to protect the number was tried and is the wrong trade -- it reads as plant sunk in a pit, and the units breaking the roofline is one of this plate's silhouette events.

featureReviews.evidence: A real leaf on a real hinge at the RIGHT jamb (X +2.89), 1.36 x 2.11 m, with stiles, rails, a glazed pane carrying the same interior image offset by the hinge, and a vertical pull bar on two stand-offs at X +1.83.
featureReviews.notes: Hung on the right because the plate's handle plate is on the LEFT of the leaf at X +1.83, which is the leading edge of a right-hung door. The template gained a `flip` flag for that -- a sign on the leaf's local x rather than a mirrored transform, because a negative scale inverts every normal on the leaf and the glass renders inside-out. It is the ONE thing on this prop that moves and the only named pivot beyond the root.

featureReviews.evidence: Pale cast stone (#a9adb1, PBR confidence 0.726) capping front, sides and rear at ONE level, y 4.44..4.60, inset from the parapet faces; plus the proud hood over the roller shutter and the plinth under the shopfront, all in the same submission.
featureReviews.notes: Grouped by MATERIAL rather than location, which is what puts a roofline coping, a hood on the +X wall and a plinth at the ground in one component. The step at the corner is gone: the side and rear runs were at 3.95..4.11 against the front's 4.44..4.60.

featureReviews.evidence: A seamless 512 tile in MULTIPLIER space -- rain streaking off the coping, patchy float marks, board-marked seams at 1.2 m and fine aggregate speckle -- repeated metrically at 3.2 m over the shell and the parapet. The lit front wall measures luma 193 against the plate's 193.
featureReviews.notes: Amplitude is the whole story here. At the first values the tile read as brushed metal, a regular vertical corduroy on every elevation, and cost 42% of the wall's linear albedo -- the front pier measured 146 against the plate's 193. Streaks halved in number and amplitude, tile widened, albedo lifted to #c8cac9 to pay for what the tile takes. Scored 0.85 and not higher because it is a procedural tile, not the plate's own dirt: the marks are the right KIND and the right strength, and they are not in the same places.
